evidence: All 13 tools use consistent snake_case function names (server.py:126 search_catalog, :200 list_datasets, :245 get_dataset, :268 get_dataset_distributions, :300 list_data_services, :343 get_data_service, :360 list_public_services, :403 list_concepts, :445 get_concept, :462 search_codelist_entries, :507 list_publishers, :551 list_catalogs, :583 api_status).
No spaces, dots, brackets or special characters in any tool name; no mixed conventions.

Descriptions are multi-sentence and carry use-case context, not just a function label (e.g. server.py:135-156 'The primary entry point: use this to find out *who* publishes data on a topic before looking for a specific dataset', server.py:307-318 'Use this to discover whether an interface already exists before building a scraper').
Tool descriptions are well over 100 chars in the median; none is a bare one-liner (server.py docstrings for all 13 tools).

Use-case framing present in prose for essentially every tool (server.py:137 'The primary entry point', :271 'This is the «where do I actually get the data» tool', :311 'The strategic payload of this server').

Caveats/important-notes are inline in docstrings where relevant (server.py:141-145 search index covers Datasets only; :275-278 licences differ per distribution; :410-414 concepts not reachable via search_catalog).
Differentiation between similar tools is explicit (search_catalog vs list_datasets at :209-212; get_dataset vs get_dataset_distributions at :249-254 and :275-278).
gaps: Use-case/important-notes information is written as prose, not as literal <use_case>/<important_notes> XML tags — accepted here under the 'oder Aequivalent' clause, but the structured-tag convention from the check example is not used.

evidence: search_catalog never returns a bare empty result: on total==0 it sets match_type='none' and an actionable hint pointing at the alternative registers (server.py:173-196).
SearchResult model carries match_type: Literal['exact','none'] and hint fields (models.py:101-108).
hint text is actionable — tells the agent the index covers Datasets only and to call list_datasets/list_concepts/list_data_services (server.py:177-182).
Covered by test test_search_empty_returns_actionable_hint (tests/test_tools.py:206-214). Data is non-sensitive public open data, so the sensitive-lookup exception does not apply.
gaps: Only search_catalog carries match_type/hint; match_type has no 'fuzzy' tier, but the upstream search offers no fuzzy capability so a partial-match fallback is not available (documented limitation).

evidence: Tool handlers take only ctx: Context for client/session info; no handler touches request.headers, websocket, stdin or stdout (server.py tool signatures; ctx used only for ctx.debug/report_progress at :114-115, :598-599).
Dual transport selectable at runtime via I14Y_MCP_TRANSPORT env var — stdio, sse and streamable-http all supported (server.py:706-722).
Shared setup (single pooled httpx client) lives in a FastMCP lifespan common to all transports (server.py:55-72, _lifespan / build_client / set_shared_client).
Tool bodies are transport-agnostic and produce identical results regardless of transport; HTTP CORS wrapping is isolated in build_http_app (server.py:674-693).
gaps: Configuration is read via scattered os.getenv() calls in main() rather than a Pydantic BaseSettings object; acceptable under the 'o.ae.' clause since config is trivial (transport/host/port/log_level) and read function-locally, not via mutable global module vars — but no formal Settings object exists.

evidence: No API keys, passwords, tokens or connection strings in source — the I14Y read API is unauthenticated (server.py:613-616, client.py has no auth headers).
No os.environ.get(..., default=secret) patterns; the only env vars are non-secret config: I14Y_MCP_TRANSPORT, LOG_LEVEL, HOST, PORT (server.py:64,705-711).
No secrets emitted to logs; structured logging only records paths/status/timings (client.py:140-189).
.gitignore contains .env (.gitignore:12); no .env file is committed.
gaps: No CI secret-scanning workflow (gitleaks/trufflehog) runs on PRs — an explicit pass-criterion, though the server has zero secret surface so the residual risk is only accidental future commits.
No .env.example present (there is nothing secret to configure, so effectively N/A).

evidence: 13 tools exposed (server.py; README.md:107-123 tool table), within the 9-15 'review the clustering' band rather than the >15 API-mapping anti-pattern zone.
Not a 1:1 REST-endpoint mapping: get_dataset aggregates the full record incl. distributions in one call so the anchor query is answered in two calls (server.py:245-264).
Tools are use-case oriented (discovery, interfaces, semantics, actors, ops groups) rather than CRUD-per-endpoint.
Anchor demo query documented as answerable via search_catalog -> get_dataset, i.e. <=2 tool calls (README.md:33-53, server.py:249-254).
gaps: 13 tools is one above the 'idealerweise <=12' guideline; justified by the distinct entity registers (datasets, data services, public services, concepts, publishers, catalogs) each needing list/detail access.

evidence: get_dataset is a genuinely aggregated tool: one call returns contact point, temporal/spatial coverage, documentation links and every distribution with its licence (server.py:245-264; models.py DatasetDetail:148-155 includes distributions).
Tools return thought-complete results, not opaque IDs requiring follow-up calls — list results carry titles/publishers/themes/landing pages (models.py summaries).

The aggregated character is called out explicitly in the description and CHANGELOG (server.py:249-254 'a single call returns ... so search_catalog -> get_dataset answers ... in two calls'; CHANGELOG Unreleased ARCH-007 entry).
gaps: No asyncio.gather parallelism, but it is unnecessary here: the upstream /datasets/{id} endpoint already returns the full aggregated record in a single HTTP call, so there is nothing to fan out.
get_dataset_distributions overlaps with get_dataset; documented as such (server.py:275-278), a minor convenience-tool redundancy rather than a chaining requirement.

evidence: Server exposes Tools only (no @mcp.resource or @mcp.prompt anywhere in src/).

evidence: CHANGELOG.md present and in Keep-a-Changelog format with SemVer statement and Unreleased/0.1.0 sections (CHANGELOG.md:1-105).

gaps: protocolVersion is NOT explicitly pinned in server code — mcp = FastMCP('i14y-mcp', lifespan=_lifespan) (server.py:72) sets no protocol_version; the README makes a deliberate choice to rely on SDK-negotiated version + floor pin instead, which does not satisfy the check's explicit-pin criterion.

The README 'MCP protocol version' section names no concrete supported spec date (e.g. 2025-06-18); CHANGELOG entries reference SDK/tooling but no explicit spec-version bump line yet (acceptable while still on floor-pin, but the explicit-version criterion is unmet).
